problem: Image-goal diffusion navigation foundation models like NoMaD do not natively support point-goal navigation, and safe navigation in constrained, cluttered indoor spaces remains hard, with frequent collisions and small clearance to obstacles.
motivation: Safely navigating cluttered indoor environments is a challenge for autonomous robots. Large-scale pretrained diffusion policies could be reused for PointGoal navigation if adapted efficiently in simulation while keeping their pretrained behavior and staying deployable on real robots.
key_idea: Replace NoMaD's image-goal conditioning with polar-coordinate point goals and finetune it on NeuralSLAM expert trajectories plus embodiment-free FMM trajectories that maximize obstacle clearance.
insight: The abstract states that finetuning with FMM-generated trajectories that maximize distance from obstacles reduces collisions and increases obstacle clearance. Performance remains stable even when the training trajectories include collisions, and the pretrained behavior is preserved. No ablation details are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Goal representation swap: replace NoMaD's image-goal encoding with polar coordinates (distance/angle) of a 2D-map point goal for PointGoal navigation.
Diffusion policy backbone: extend NoMaD, a diffusion-based navigation foundation model pretrained on a large-scale real-world dataset.
Expert trajectory finetuning: finetune using expert trajectories from NeuralSLAM in simulation.
Embodiment-free FMM trajectories: generate trajectories with the Fast Marching Method that maximize distance from obstacles, used as additional finetuning data.
Real-world deployment: run on a Kachaka robot for short-range navigation.

setting.training_data: NoMaD pretraining on a large-scale real-world dataset, then finetuning on simulated expert trajectories from NeuralSLAM and FMM-generated embodiment-free trajectories (scale not given)
setting.observation: egocentric visual observations plus a point goal in polar coordinates
setting.action_space: predicted trajectories/waypoints from a diffusion policy
setting.privileged: FMM trajectory generation uses map information at training time; none stated at test time

results: The abstract reports a reduced collision rate, increased distance to obstacles, and stable performance even with collision-containing training trajectories, without giving numbers. Real-world tests on a Kachaka robot show effective short-range navigation.
limitations: Real-world validation is limited to short-range navigation.
Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and baselines are unknown.
